newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 12.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 12.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON - Advertising and marketing company WPP Group Plc says its wholly owned subsidiary, the Ogilvy Group Inc, has acquired the outstanding 28 percent of the ordinary shares in Ogilvy & Mather Argentina S.A.. WPP has paid an initial consideration of 1.5 million Argentine pesos ($1.5 million). A further consideration of 500,000 pesos may also be payable within three years.

CANBERRA - The Australian government launches a national anti-smoking campaign worth A$7 ($5.26) million over the next two financial years. The campaign includes television commercials, print advertisements and practical support for smokers wanting to quit.

LONDON - Saatchi & Saatchi advertising agency launches a cause-related marketing unit to identify and build links between charities and businesses."Cause- related marketing is the ultimate in feel-good marketing and is something that consumers actually want. We anticipate that it will be an area of huge growth and value to our clients," says Alan Bishop, chairman of Saatchi & Saatchi in the UK.

NEW YORK - Absolut, whose vodka marketing has turned the outline of a bottle into an advertising icon, plans a Father's Day newspaper ad with the message, "You're one in a million. Happy Father's Day," will be placed in 250,000 home-delivered copies of this Sunday's New York Times.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
PARIS - French newspapers had strong advertising income in the first quarter of 1997, with La Liberation, Le Monde and La Tribune faring better than most dailies, a top executive at Liberation said.

LONDON- British leisure and television group Granada Group Plc says it has no current plans to demerge its media businesses. Granada chairman Gerry Robinson says there may be some point in the future when the media interests could be split off, but says that point has not been reached.
KRONBERG - The German radio market has expanded again this year, with over 80 percent of adults listening to the radio every day, says the German unit of media marketing company IP.

REDWOOD CITY, California - Intuit Inc will make a $40 million equity investment in Excite Inc as part of a seven-year agreement to programme, promote and distribute a new online financial channel, the companies say.

PARIS - Talks over U.S. media company Time Warner Inc buying France's Cie Generale des Eaux's cable television unit are continuing, Jean-Marie Messier, chairman of Generale des Eaux, tells the company's annual meeting.
NEW YORK - Paxson Communications Corp and Bloomberg LP say they have a deal to air Bloomberg Television on New York WPXN-TV, Channel 31, 12 hours a day.

KINGSTON, Jamaica - The state-owned Jamaica Broadcasting Corporation has been sold for $2 million to publicly-traded Radio Jamaica, largely ending the Jamaican government's involvement in the media, officials announce.
PARIS - French public television channel France 2 declines comment on a report in Le Monde newspaper that it will show a loss of at least 70 million francs ($12 million) for 1996.
LONDON - UK commercial radio company GWR Group Plc says it is launching its own in-house advertising sales unit.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - The price of shares in British food and drinks group Cadbury Schweppes Plc climbs after the Wall Street Journal says Coca-Cola Co might increase its prices after July 4, potentially ending the price war in the U.S. soft drink
industry.
BRUSSELS - New car registrations in western Europe dropped 1.9 percent year-on-year in May to 1,151,900 units, the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association says.

LONDON - Britons can now reach for a new thirst quencher -- hemp-flavoured soda. But those seeking the effects of marijuana, hemp's illicit derivative, should not get their hopes too high. The citrus soda is called Hemp, but all psychoactive substances have been weeded out, according to Shackleford Sales Ltd, which imports the German-owned brand.
SINGAPORE - Japan's Fujitsu Ltd aims to double its sales of telecommunications and information products in the booming Asian market, president Tadashi Sekizawa says.

BRUSSELS - Jaguar Cars Ltd expects its X200 model -- the smallest it has ever produced -- to spur sales on to over 90,000 in 1999, more than double last year's 40,000, chairman and chief executive Nick Scheele says.
OAK BROOK, Illinois - McDonald's Corp says it plans to open its first restaurant in Cyprus. With the opening, the company will have operations in 103 countries.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

SANTIAGO - Consumers have got a taste for Chilean wine and as a result exports soared 65 percent in the first quarter of the year to $79.6 million over the same period last year, the Agriculture Ministry reports. The U.S. continues to be the largest market for Chilean wine, followed by Britain at $8.2 million and Denmark at $3.2 million.

MEXICO CITY - Mexican consumers are struggling with mountains of debt. The amount of consumer debt, including credit card and durable good loans, owed to banks in December 1996 totalled 8.0 billion pesos ($1 billion), according to economic experts.
BEIJING - Stamp dealers in China's capital are cashing in on the imminent end to more than 150 years of British colonial rule over Hong Kong with buyers snapping up postal souvenirs,
officials say.
